newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Treasury flush with funds, supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Treasury flush with funds, supply tight.

text.p: The Portuguese Treasury is flush with funds so that the supply of paper will remain fairly tight through the remainder of the year, helping underpin the market's recent strength, analysts said.

Some analysts forecast that providing the optimism over the chances of Spain and Portugal joining Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) remains undiminished, the spread with the German 10-year cash bunds could reach 125 basis points by the year's end. It stood at just under 150 basis points on Wednesday.
The Treasury has so far issued some 719 billion escudos of the 790 billion escudos planned for the whole of 1996.

"The normal levels of emission for the three, five and 10 years are being fulfilled and there should be no supply pressure (over the remainder of the year)," said Mario Diaz Vigario of Morgan Grenfell in Lisbon.
Demonstrating its lack of urgency for financing, the Treasury accepted bids for only half of the offered 20 billion escudos of its February 2006 paper at the latest sale on Tuesday.
A relative supply shortage has been a factor helping the Portuguese market keep pace with the Spanish bonos as they hit record highs on confidence that the two countries will qualify for EMU.
Analysts noted that a change this year in the financing regulations meant that unlike in past years, there would be no last minute rush on the part of the Treasury to finance itself.

Previously, the Treasury was obliged to raise funds it needed to pay commitments falling due in January, but relating to expenditure authorised for the previous year, by the end of the preceding December.
But now the funds themselves can be raised in the month in which payment is due.
Sources close the Treasury estimated that such funding normally amounted to around 80-100 billion escudos and tended to bloat the market with supply around the end of the year.
